title: feat(spec,drivers,objectql,analytics,formula): $icontains reaches every JS evaluation face (#6520)
body:
Closes #6520

The other half of #5702. That change implemented `$icontains` on the SQL family and correctly left the spec's `FILTER_OPERATORS` alone; this one adds the operator to that array and gives **every remaining evaluation face** an arm — in one PR, because those two steps cannot be separated.

## The ruling chain

**Maintainer ruling, 2026-08-08 (Option A — approved), quoted from the card:**

> **Maintainer ruling (2026-08-08): Option A — approved.** Add $icontains to the spec FILTER_OPERATORS word list and bring every JS evaluation face up to parity, as a sanctioned one-off exception to the #5499 investment freeze, strictly for semantic parity — not new capability.
>
> Hard constraints for the dispatch (from the card, now binding):
> - **Single PR, whole batch**: spec word list + driver-memory (both faces) + driver-mongodb + service-analytics + objectql having + formula, plus conformance coverage. The word list must NOT land ahead of the evaluators — that would flip the JS faces' fail-closed refusal into silent acceptance, the #3948 RLS-bypass shape.
> - **The PR body must declare a conclusion for every compile face** per the face-inventory clause in the dispatch playbook (changed / already compliant with evidence / explicitly out of scope with reason). The frozen driver-memory / driver-mongodb faces are being changed here under the sanctioned exception, so they report as changed.

The maintainer directive recorded on that comment is quoted verbatim and untranslated: 「你的建议全部接受」.

**Census note, 2026-08-09 (#6993), quoted from the card:**

> #6993 普查实测补一格（2026-08-09，`origin/main` @ `08863dd18`，执行测量）：本卡现状表中 `@objectstack/formula` `matchesFilter` 一行标 ❌ 与其余拒收面并列，但它的「❌」与其他面**不同类**：
>
> - `matchesFilterCondition({ name: 'ACME CORP' }, { name: { $icontains: 'acme' } })` → **静默返回 `false`**（`evalOp` 的 `default: return false; // unknown operator → fail closed`），不抛错、无 code、无 message；`$regex` 同样静默 `false`。
> - 其余 JS 面（driver-memory 两面、driver-mongodb、objectql `having`）均**响亮拒收**（throw；信封状态见 #7047）。
>
> 即 formula 面对一个 spec 已声明的算子给出的是「无声的否答」，不是「fail-closed 拒收」—— 恰是 #4706 对旧 `$regex` 的第二项指控（illegal pattern → `return false`）在这一面的残留形态。给 formula 加 `$icontains` 臂时（本卡范围第 4 条），建议同 PR 决定 unknown-`$` 算子在该面是维持静默 `false` 还是升级为 throw，并把决定写进 `matches-filter.ts` 的 docblock；`filter.zod.ts` 的 "The other JS evaluators sit on the refusing side too" 一句对 formula 的措辞也应随之校正。

## Premise verification (on `origin/main` @ `f5a9bc2f3`)

Every claim in the card re-measured before implementing; all held.

| card's claim | measured |
|---|---|
| `FILTER_OPERATORS` lacks `$icontains` | held — `filter.zod.ts:1356`, 15 members, no `$icontains` |
| vocabulary pin fixes the diff set at exactly `{$icontains}` | held — `filter-operator-vocabulary.test.ts:60` `toEqual(['$icontains'])` |
| SQL family evaluates with ASCII-only folding | held — `sql-driver.ts:1379-1382`, Postgres `translate(expr,'A..Z','a..z')` on both sides |
| driver-memory refuses via a gate derived from `FILTER_OPERATORS` | held — `filter-refusal.ts:178` `new Set([...FILTER_OPERATORS])` |
| driver-mongodb refuses at its translator `default:` | held — `mongodb-filter.ts:590` |
| objectql `having` refuses (`CONDITION_OPERATORS`) | held — `having-filter.ts:60` |
| formula answers a silent `false`, a different class | held — `matches-filter.ts` `evalOp` `default: return false` |

One scope correction the card's estimate did not carry: item 3 says "add an arm to `compileScopedFilterToSql`", but the echo-coverage test drives **three** compilers off `FILTER_OPERATORS` (`compileScopedFilterToSql`, `NativeSQLStrategy`, `ObjectQLStrategy.generateSql`) plus `filter-normalizer.ts`'s `MONGO_TO_CUBE_OP`. All four are changed here; leaving any one out fails that test.

## Face inventory — a conclusion for every compile/evaluation face

**Changed (under the sanctioned #5499 exception):**

| face | file | what it does now |
|---|---|---|
| spec word list | `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts` | `FILTER_OPERATORS` admits `$icontains`; staging docblock rewritten |
| spec shared fold | same file | new `foldAsciiCase` / `asciiCaseInsensitiveContains` / `asciiCaseInsensitiveRegexSource` |
| driver-memory query path | `memory-driver.ts` | mingo `$regex` from the ASCII pattern source, **no `i` flag** |
| driver-memory reference matcher | `memory-matcher.ts` | `asciiCaseInsensitiveContains` |
| driver-memory analytics (cube) face | `memory-analytics.ts` | new `icontains` cube operator + predicate builder + SQL row |
| driver-memory shape gate | `filter-refusal.ts` | admits by derivation; new non-empty-string comparand rule |
| driver-mongodb | `mongodb-filter.ts` | `$regex` with the ASCII pattern and **no `$options`**; comparand rule on the walk |
| objectql `having` | `having-filter.ts` | `asciiCaseInsensitiveContains` |
| formula (RLS write `check`) | `matches-filter.ts` | `asciiCaseInsensitiveContains` + the posture decision below |
| service-analytics normalizer | `strategies/filter-normalizer.ts` | `$icontains` maps to the `icontains` leaf |
| service-analytics RLS lowering | `read-scope-sql.ts` | folded `LIKE`, both sides |
| service-analytics native SQL | `strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts` | folded `LIKE`, both sides |
| service-analytics `/analytics/sql` echo | `strategies/objectql-strategy.ts` | folded `LIKE`, both sides |
| conformance ledger | `scripts/check-driver-conformance.mjs` | requirement-1 half cleared on both DEBT rows |

**Already compliant — evidence, not assumption:**

- `driver-sql`, `driver-sqlite-wasm`, `driver-turso` (local + remote): implemented by #5702/#6518. Unchanged here; their suites re-run green. This PR's fold is deliberately character-identical to `sql-driver.ts`'s Postgres arm.
- `packages/lint`'s RLS predicate rules: they consult `isSupportedRlsExpression` / `compileCelToFilter`, not the operator table — no operator vocabulary of their own to widen.
- `spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`'s `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS`: a **separate** authoring vocabulary for view filters, not derived from `FILTER_OPERATORS`. Untouched deliberately — the view authoring surface is #6337's lane, not this one.

**Out of scope, with reason:**

- The `$contains` family folding the whole Unicode range on driver-memory's query path and driver-mongodb — that is **#6682**, requirement 2 of the same case-set, and it is why both conformance DEBT rows survive this PR instead of being deleted.
- `formula`'s silent `false` for **retired** spellings (`$regex` / `$options`) — see the posture section.

## The #3948 probe — direction predicted first, then measured

PREDICTION, written before running: with the word list admitted and `memory-matcher.ts`'s arm reverted, the matcher's `default: break` treats the operator as "no constraint", so the reference matcher should answer **EVERY row** — a silent widening, not a throw — and the new pins should go red on the row-set assertion rather than on a missing error.

MEASURED on this branch — `git checkout origin/main -- memory-matcher.ts` (never `git stash`: `refs/stash` is shared by every worktree of this repo, objectui#3430), then run `match()` over the conformance fixture, then `git checkout HEAD --` to restore:

```
rows returned : ["1","2","3","4","5","6","7","8","9"]
fixture size  : 9
VERDICT       : MATCH-ALL - predicate silently DROPPED (#3948)
a NON-match row ("zzz") answers: true
```

**The prediction held exactly, including the direction.** The face does not refuse and does not error — it answers `true` for a row that plainly does not contain `acme`, which is #5701's measurement reproduced on this branch rather than quoted from it. The gate accepts the operator because `SUPPORTED_FIELD_OPERATORS` *is* `FILTER_OPERATORS`, and the matcher's `default:` arm `break`s, which means "no constraint".

So the loudness lives in the TESTS, not in the runtime: `memory-icontains.test.ts` asserts exact row-id lists, so this state fails it on the ROW SET (9 ids where 2 were expected) — which is why those pins assert ids rather than `toThrow()`. A throw-only assertion would have stayed green against a face that silently matched everything, and that is precisely the shape it would have missed.

This is also the answer to "why one PR": there is no ordering in which the word list lands first and the failure is visible. It is not a refusal, not an error, and not a smaller row set — it is a permission-shaped widening that looks like a working filter.

## Folding parity — same answers as SQL

Every face is driven over `FILTER_TEXT_ROWS` — the conformance standard's own fixture — so the answers are comparable to the SQL family's by construction. Predictions written before the suites were run, from the contract rather than from the implementation:

| filter | predicted ids | why that is the contract |
|---|---|---|
| `{ $icontains: 'acme' }` | `1, 2` | the fold runs on BOTH sides, so `ACME Corp` matches a lower-case comparand |
| `{ $icontains: 'ACME' }` | `1, 2` | and the mirror direction |
| `{ $icontains: 'café' }` | `4` only | ASCII-ONLY: `É` does not fold, so `CAFÉ` must NOT match (#4706 Q1 = A) |
| `{ $icontains: 'CAFÉ' }` | `3` only | the mirror — exactly one row survives each direction |
| `{ $icontains: '100%' }` | `5` only | comparand is LITERAL: `%` is not a wildcard |
| `{ $icontains: 'a_b' }` | `7` only | `_` is not a wildcard |
| `{ $icontains: 'a.b' }` | `9` only | `.` is not a regex metacharacter — the `$regex` defect, restated |

The two non-ASCII rows are the load-bearing ones: a face that reached for `toLowerCase()` or a `RegExp` with the `i` flag answers `3, 4` to BOTH and is wrong twice. That is the only way to tell an ASCII fold from a Unicode one by row set.

MEASURED on this branch, by running each face over the fixture — **every prediction held, on every face**:

```
comparand | mem-matcher | having | formula
"acme"    | 1,2         | 1,2    | 1,2
"ACME"    | 1,2         | 1,2    | 1,2
"café"    | 4           | 4      | 4
"CAFÉ"    | 3           | 3      | 3
"100%"    | 5           | 5      | 5
"a_b"     | 7           | 7      | 7
"a.b"     | 9           | 9      | 9

$contains "acme" (must stay case-exact): matcher=2 formula=2
```

driver-memory's query path and analytics face are held to the same row sets by `memory-icontains.test.ts` (which asserts the two faces answer identically, case by case) and by the analytics face's own declared-operator probe; driver-mongodb by `mongodb-icontains.test.ts`, which executes the emitted pattern over the same fixture.

On the SQL side the parity is structural rather than statistical — the emitted statement is character-identical in construct to `driver-sql`'s Postgres arm. Measured by calling `compileScopedFilterToSql` directly on this branch:

```
$icontains "acme"
  sql   : translate("person"."name", 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ', 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz') LIKE translate(?, 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ', 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz') ESCAPE ?
  params: ["%acme%","\\"]
$icontains "100%"
  params: ["%100\\%%","\\"]
$icontains "a_b"
  params: ["%a\\_b%","\\"]
```

Both sides folded; the comparand still escaped and the `ESCAPE` character still bound, so the fold rides ON TOP of the literal-comparand rule rather than replacing it. `translate()` with an explicit 26-character domain is used rather than `LOWER()` precisely because Postgres' `LOWER()` is locale-aware and would fold `É`.

Additionally pinned per face, because a fold is easy to add and easy to over-apply: `$contains` stays case-SENSITIVE on the faces that already had it right (the reference matcher, `having`, `formula`), and driver-mongodb's `$contains` family still emits its hardcoded `$options: 'i'` — pinned as the CURRENT state so that fixing #6682 and breaking `$icontains` can never be confused for one another.

## The formula posture decision (census note)

**Decision: keep the silent, fail-closed `false` for unknown operators; documented in `matches-filter.ts`'s header.** Reasons, in the order they carry weight:

1. The error direction is opposite on this face. The other five faces compile READ predicates, where a dropped constraint WIDENS (#3948) and must be loud. This one evaluates a WRITE-side `check`: an unevaluable condition DENIES the write. Silence costs a diagnostic, not a boundary.
2. Callers rely on it being TOTAL — `plugin-security`'s `explain-engine` calls it per record with no `catch`, and several driver doubles use it as a list filter. Throwing turns a per-record verdict into an aborted operation on the read/explain path, which is not what a `$icontains` parity PR should be deciding.
3. The census's measured defect is gone without the upgrade: every operator `FILTER_OPERATORS` declares now has an arm, so the silent answer is reachable only for a name the protocol never declared or has retired.

Left open **on the record** rather than folded in: a retired `$regex` / `$options` still gets the silent `false` here while the other five faces print the prescription naming `$icontains`. That changes an accept/reject surface and belongs to the maintainer, not to a parity PR. `filter.zod.ts`'s "The other JS evaluators sit on the refusing side too" sentence — which mis-described this face — is corrected.

## Downstream

#5814 (better-auth `Where.mode: 'insensitive'`) had its blocker cleared: an authentication query using `$icontains` no longer 400s on the in-memory double.

### Three gates fired during development, and all three were right

Recorded because a gate that catches you is evidence the gate works, and the first two of these are the mechanism this PR is about:

1. **`check:driver-conformance` — RECONCILED.** The first version of the driver-memory suite mentioned the text case-set's marker export in its *docblock prose*. The gate matches an import span loosely, read that as "this driver now runs the case-set", and failed because a ledger entry for a covered cell is an error. Correct: requirement 2 of that case-set is still open here (#6682), so this driver must NOT claim the whole set. Fixed by driving `FILTER_TEXT_ROWS` and never naming the marker; both DEBT rows survive, each now naming one open requirement instead of two.
2. **driver-memory's declared-operator probe gate.** `memory-driver-filter-logic-conformance.test.ts` keys a probe map by the analytics face's OWN declared vocabulary and fails when a declared operator has no probe. Adding `$icontains` to `MONGO_TO_CUBE_OPERATOR` turned it red immediately — which is exactly the guarantee #5374 bought. The probe added for it uses an UPPER-case comparand (`'BET'`) against a lower-case fixture row (`beta`), so it only selects a row once the fold actually runs; a lower-case comparand would have agreed across the two faces for free even if neither folded, the free-agreement certification that block's own header warns against.
3. **`check:api-surface` — the SECOND export snapshot.** Regenerating `export-origins/` is not enough: `api-surface/` is a separate artifact tracking the public NAME SET (plus factory signatures), and it went red on CI with `0 breaking (removed/narrowed), 3 added`. Fixed with `gen:api-surface`; the delta is exactly the three additive `./data` exports. Recorded because "I regenerated the export snapshot" is precisely the reasoning that misses it — there are two, and adding an export touches both. The rest of that family (`check:exported-any`, `check:dual-source-exports`, `check:docs`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:skill-refs`, `check:react-blocks`) was then swept in one pass rather than one CI lap at a time, and is green.

## Out-of-scope finding filed

- **#7117** — driver-memory's analytics `generateSql()` renders the LIKE family with no wildcards, so the echoed statement is an equality the pipeline never ran. Pre-existing, affects `$contains` / `$notContains`; the `icontains` row added here is consistent with its neighbour and inherits the same defect (it was added so the operator would not fall to the `|| '='` fallback, which would be strictly worse).
